T: Faith is believing. Dinner is eating.
D: A kindly old man hired as a department store Santa insists he's the real thing, and ends up in court.
P: Serve the mains when Kris shares Thanksgiving dinner with Doris and Susan.
S: Parade chestnuts in sage brown butter
Roasted chestnuts peeled warm and tossed in sage brown butter

Chestnuts scored and roasted until they split, peeled warm and tossed in nutty brown butter with crisp sage, maple and flaky salt. Cut a cross in the flat side of 600g chestnuts and soak in water for 10 minutes. Roast at 220C for 25 minutes until the shells open, then wrap in a tea towel for 5 minutes and peel while warm. Melt 60g butter until it foams and turns nutty brown, add 12 sage leaves and fry until crisp. Toss in the chestnuts with 1 tbsp maple syrup and flaky salt.
the long line to sit on Santa's knee

Brown butter shortbread rounds dipped in white chocolate and crushed candy cane, the kind Kris might hand out to the children in line. Brown 200g butter until nutty, chill until soft-set, then beat with 90g caster sugar. Mix in 250g plain flour, 30g cornflour and a pinch of salt. Roll into a log, chill 30 minutes, slice into 20 rounds and bake at 160C for 18 minutes. Cool, dip half of each in 150g melted white chocolate and sprinkle with crushed candy cane.
Celery filled with cream cheese and blue cheese, crackers topped with cheddar

Celery sticks filled with cream cheese whipped with blue cheese and chives, and crackers with sharp cheddar. Beat 250g cream cheese with 50g blue cheese and snipped chives until smooth. Cut celery into short sticks and pipe or spoon the filling along each. Serve on a platter beside crackers topped with slices of vintage cheddar, the way a 1940s party did it.
M: the Thanksgiving Kris spends with Doris and Susan

Brined turkey breast roasted juicy with herb butter, cornbread and sage stuffing, buttery mash, cranberry sauce and a deep pan gravy. Brine a 1.5kg turkey breast roll in 2 litres water with 100g salt and 50g sugar overnight. Pat dry, rub with 50g herb butter and roast at 170C to 70C inside, about 80 minutes. Rest 15 minutes. Bake 300g crumbled cornbread with 1 diced onion softened in butter, sage, 1 egg and 150ml stock for 30 minutes. Mash 1kg potatoes with butter and milk. Make gravy from the tray juices, flour and 300ml stock.
Fred Gailey's New York pot roast
Beef chuck braised in red wine with carrots, celery and potatoes

Beef chuck seared, onion, carrot and celery, red wine and stock, braised at 160C for 3 hours, potatoes for the last hour. Sear a 1.5kg piece of beef chuck all over. Add a sliced onion, 3 carrots and 2 celery sticks, then 250ml red wine and enough water to come halfway. Cover and braise at 160C for 3 hours, adding 800g potatoes for the last hour. Slice and serve with the juices.
W: Brandy-soaked fruit pudding steamed for 4 hours, flamed with warm brandy
Dried fruit soaked overnight in brandy, mixed with butter, brown sugar, eggs, breadcrumbs, flour and spice, steamed 4 hours, flamed at the table. Custard.
K: Apple juice simmered with maple, cinnamon, star anise, cloves and orange

Cloudy apple juice mulled with maple, cinnamon, star anise and orange, ladled steaming into mugs with a cinnamon stick and a clove-studded orange slice. Pour 1.5 litres cloudy apple juice into a pot with 3 tbsp maple syrup, 2 cinnamon sticks, 3 star anise, 6 cloves and 1 sliced orange. Bring to a simmer, then keep just below simmering for 20 minutes. Strain into mugs and add a cinnamon stick and an orange slice studded with cloves to each.
